task.description:
WF-03 Step 3 security gate (WF-02 Step 2c equivalent) on the ISS-0106 fix. Review `git diff main...HEAD`, restricted to the source changes -- the handoff JSONs, the design markdown and the decision record in that diff are audit-trail artefacts, not executable surface.

WHAT THE CHANGE IS, so your scope test starts from facts rather than the file list: three parts. (A) toolchain pin and a NEW mix task at lib/mix/tasks/letflow.check_toolchain.ex that reads .tool-versions and prints an advisory warning; plus README/developer-guide text. (B) four files reformatted by `mix format` -- whitespace and line wrapping only. (C) sixteen struct-update annotation sites across lib/letflow/engine/{transition,reconstruction,sub_process}.ex and lib/letflow/engine.ex.

Run your own scope test and state the verdict either way -- 'not in scope' is a legitimate and useful result here, but it must be reached by applying the test, not by reading this description and agreeing with it.

TWO THINGS DESERVE REAL SCRUTINY RATHER THAN A NOT-APPLICABLE SWEEP, because a change that is cosmetic in intent can still be substantive in effect:

  1. **Part C is claimed to be an annotation-only change, and that claim is worth testing rather than accepting.** The idiom adds an explicit struct pattern (`%InstanceState{} = instance_state`) at a BIND site where previously a bare variable was bound. A bare variable binds anything; a struct pattern RAISES MatchError when the value is not that struct. So at each of the sixteen sites, the change is behaviour-preserving only if the value at that point is always already that struct on every reachable path -- including error paths, reconstruction-from-event-log paths, and any path that could carry a plain map (for example a decoded JSON payload or a serialised event) rather than a struct. If any site can receive a non-struct on a real path, this change converts a silent proceed into a raise. These are engine files on the instance-execution path, so the blast radius of a wrong one is a crashed instance process, not a formatting nit. Sample the sites -- you need not exhaustively prove all sixteen -- and state which you examined and what you found.

  2. **The new mix task reads a file from the repo and prints its contents into a warning.** It is developer tooling and not a request path, so most invariants will be NOT-APPLICABLE. Still check what it actually does with what it reads: whether any value it prints could be attacker-influenced in a realistic scenario, whether it can be made to read a path other than the project-root .tool-versions, and INV-4 specifically (it touches no secrets by design -- confirm that by reading it rather than by assuming, since it does perform file I/O and string interpolation into output).

Record a verdict per invariant, INV-1 through INV-8, marking each APPLIES or NOT-APPLICABLE explicitly -- an unlisted invariant reads as an unrun check, per the worked example in docs/agents/shared/HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md §2.

One fact you should have rather than rediscover: ELIXIR-DEV reports `mix letflow.check` currently exits 1 at its `letflow.check.test` step with 14 test failures, and reports having attributed them as pre-existing by stashing its own changes back to HEAD and re-running against the same database (identical result). Attribution of those failures belongs to TEST-RUNNER at Step 4 and is not your gate -- do not chase it. It matters to you only if you find reason to believe a failure is caused by one of the sixteen Part C sites, which would make it a behaviour change rather than an annotation.
acceptance_criteria: The scope test is stated and applied explicitly, with the verdict (in scope / not in scope) and the reasoning -- not assumed from the task description
A verdict is recorded for every invariant INV-1 through INV-8, each marked APPLIES or NOT-APPLICABLE, with a PASS/FAIL for those that apply

Part C's behaviour-preservation claim is tested rather than accepted: state which of the sixteen sites you examined, how you determined the value at that bind site is always the expected struct on every reachable path, and the verdict. If you cannot establish it for a site, say so plainly rather than passing it

lib/mix/tasks/letflow.check_toolchain.ex is reviewed for what it reads, what it interpolates into output, and whether its file lookup can be redirected; INV-4 assessed against the actual code rather than its stated intent
Any finding is reported with severity and the specific file:line, and a FAIL names what must change
No file outside handoffs/ is modified by this step

result.summary:
SECURITY-REVIEWER gate on the ISS-0106 fix: PASS. Scope test applied to `git diff main...HEAD` (source files only; the handoff JSONs, lib/letflow/design/iss0106-*.md and docs/migration/decisions/0005-*.md are audit-trail artefacts, not executable surface).

SCOPE TEST, applied criterion by criterion rather than assumed from the task description:
(1) API route reading/writing tenant-scoped data added or modified? NO -- no file under a router/controller/plug surface is in the diff; S4 has not started.
(2) priv/repo/migrations/*.exs added or modified? NO -- the diff contains no migration.
(3) Anything resolving a secret (config, env var, token) added or modified? YES, potentially: lib/mix/tasks/letflow.check_toolchain.ex is a NEW file that performs file I/O and interpolates what it reads into output. This is the criterion that pulls the diff into scope and it was checked against the code, not its stated intent (see INV-4).
(4) Response-shaping code for a tenant-scoped entity added or modified? NO.
(5) Lookup-by-ID handler added or modified? NO new handler; however lib/letflow/engine.ex, engine/transition.ex, engine/reconstruction.ex and engine/sub_process.ex ARE on the instance-execution path and do read/write tenant-scoped rows through Ecto `:prefix`, so INV-1 is run against them rather than skipped.

SCOPE VERDICT: IN SCOPE, on criteria (3) and (5)-adjacent. Not a not-applicable sweep. Full per-invariant verdicts are in result.issues[] as INFO records so each is explicitly on the record: INV-1 APPLIES/PASS, INV-2 NOT-APPLICABLE, INV-3 NOT-APPLICABLE, INV-4 APPLIES/PASS, INV-5 NOT-APPLICABLE, INV-6 APPLIES/PASS, INV-7 APPLIES/PASS, INV-8 APPLIES/PASS. No FAIL on any applicable invariant, so no BLOCKER and no routing back to ELIXIR-DEV.

PART C (the sixteen struct-pattern bind sites) -- TESTED, NOT ACCEPTED. Counted and confirmed sixteen: engine.ex 1, reconstruction.ex 7, sub_process.ex 1, transition.ex 7. The claim under test was that adding an explicit struct pattern at a site that previously bound a bare variable is behaviour-preserving, which is only true if the value is already that struct on every reachable path. Examined all sixteen statically and traced producers to closure for the four highest-risk classes; verdict: behaviour-preserving, with the failure mode at each site correctly identified as unreachable rather than merely unlikely.

  RISK CLASS 1 -- snapshot-seeded replay (reconstruction.ex, 5 apply_event/4 clauses + resolve_pending_events/1). This is the exact hazard named in the task: a decoded-JSON path that could carry a plain map. reconstruction.ex:514 seeds replay from `{:from_snapshot, state_snapshot, _}`, whose sole producer is select_replay_source/2 (:451) -> SnapshotWriter.latest_snapshot/2 (snapshot_writer.ex:211). That function's only non-error return is `deserialize_state(instance_id, state)` (snapshot_writer.ex:263), which constructs an `%InstanceState{}` LITERAL, with `tokens`/`pending_task_nodes` built by token_from_map/1 (`%Token{}` literal, :288) and `join_counters` by join_counter_entry_from_map/1 (`%JoinCounter{}` literal, :297). The JSON is re-hydrated into structs AT THE STORAGE BOUNDARY, so no plain map ever reaches apply_event/4. The other seed branch, seed_instance_state/2 (:528), is likewise an `%InstanceState{}` literal. fold_events/3 (:550) then threads only apply_event's own `{:ok, new_state}`, closing the induction.
    NOTE ON THE FAILURE MODE AT THIS SITE, since it is NOT MatchError and is worth stating precisely: apply_event/4 has a catch-all final clause at reconstruction.ex:693 returning `{:error, {:unrecognized_event_type, ...}}`. Had a non-InstanceState been reachable, the five annotated clauses would have silently FALLEN THROUGH to that catch-all and mis-reported a well-formed INSTANCE_STARTED/TASK_COMPLETED event as an unrecognised event type -- a silent wrong-answer, strictly worse than a raise. It is unreachable per the trace above, but this is the site that would have justified a FAIL had the trace not closed.
    resolve_pending_events/1 (:824) has only `{:ok, %InstanceState{} = state, _}` and `{:error, _}` clauses, so a hypothetical `{:ok, non_struct, events}` would now raise FunctionClauseError rather than pass silently. Its three call sites (:571, :782, :802) are fed by Transition/SubProcess dispatch functions, all @spec'd `{:ok, InstanceState.t(), [pending_event()]}` and all returning `%InstanceState{}` literals.
  RISK CLASS 2 -- transition.ex instance_state sites (5). Decisive and simple: the module's public entry point, Transition.transition/3 at transition.ex:175, ALREADY required `%InstanceState{} = instance_state` BEFORE this change. Every annotated private callee receives instance_state transitively from that already-guarded parameter or from `%InstanceState{}` literals built inside the module. These five annotations are provably redundant, which is precisely what "annotation-only" is supposed to mean.
  RISK CLASS 3 -- transition.ex `%JoinCounter{} = counter` in dispatch_cancel_branch/3's case (:894). Enumerated every writer of `join_counters` across lib/letflow/: transition.ex:693 (`%JoinCounter{}` literal, :685), :786 and :902 (`%JoinCounter{counter | ...}` updates), snapshot_writer.ex:270 (struct literal), and four empty-map initialisers (instance_state.ex:65, reconstruction.ex:634, sub_process.ex:1103, engine.ex:1620). No writer can place a non-JoinCounter value. The `nil` case is already handled by the preceding clause. Precedent: transition.ex:778 already matched `with %JoinCounter{} = counter <- Map.get(...)` before this change.
  RISK CLASS 4 -- engine.ex:1775 and sub_process.ex:825 seed_state sites. engine.ex: `snapshot_and_state` is an Ecto.Multi step result whose sole successful producer builds the map at :1529 with `seed_instance_state: build_instance_state(...)`, and build_instance_state/3 (:1609) returns an `%InstanceState{}` literal. Conclusive precedent: engine.ex:1467 ALREADY destructured that same map key as `%InstanceState{} = seed_instance_state` before this change, so a non-struct there would have been raising already. sub_process.ex:825's seed_state arrives from :770's `{:ok, graph, node, seed_state, ...}`, produced only at :1097 as an `%InstanceState{}` literal.
  Also checked: `{:ok, %Token{} = parked_token} <-` (reconstruction.ex:668) sits inside a `with`, so a non-match would NOT raise -- it would return the unmatched value. Its producer find_sub_process_completion_token/3 (:717) returns tokens filtered out of state.tokens, whose producers are the `%Token{}` literals already enumerated.

  EMPIRICAL CORROBORATION of the static trace, since a trace alone is an argument and not evidence: ran `mix test test/letflow/engine/` on the branch -- "Result: 372 passed (1 property, 371 tests)", zero failures, 48.3s. Ran the full suite -- "Result: 1217/1230 passed (5/5 properties, 1212/1225 tests)", 465.1s. Zero MatchError, FunctionClauseError or CaseClauseError anywhere in the output (grepped explicitly for all three). The 13 observed failures are confined to Mix.Tasks.Letflow.Check.TestTest (3) and Letflow.IdentityMigrationTest (10) -- NO failure touches engine.ex, transition.ex, reconstruction.ex or sub_process.ex. Per the handoff, attribution of those failures is TEST-RUNNER's at Step 4 and was not chased; the only reason they mattered to this gate was whether any was caused by a Part C site, and none is. Materially, the test log shows `SELECT ... FROM "tenant_..."."instance_state_snapshots" ... ORDER BY sequence_number DESC LIMIT 1` executing during the run, confirming the snapshot-seeded replay path -- risk class 1, the riskiest -- is actually exercised by the passing suite and not merely reasoned about.

  ONE OBSERVATION, NOT A FINDING: the annotations are applied inconsistently -- dispatch_parallel_gateway/4 (transition.ex:605) annotates both instance_state and token, while dispatch_parallel_split/4 (:656) annotates only instance_state and leaves token bare. Harmless and out of this gate's scope; noted for REVIEWER at the idiom gate rather than filed as an issue.

PART B (the four `mix format` reformats) -- inspected the diff hunks in pin_resolver.ex, variable_merge.ex and the two test files. Whitespace, line wrapping, and one escaping change inside a `@moduledoc` code fence (variable_merge.ex:92,98, `"""` -> `\"""`). No executable semantics altered. Note that variable_merge.ex's change edits a documented grep recipe's own text; that is a doc-content question for REVIEWER, not a security one.

PART A (.tool-versions pin 1.18.3-otp-27 -> 1.20.3-otp-29, mix.exs alias, README/guide text) -- no security surface. The mix.exs change prepends `letflow.check_toolchain` to the `letflow.check` alias, ahead of `format --check-formatted` and `compile --warnings-as-errors`. Checked specifically against core-directives.md's "Never Satisfy a Gate by Editing What It Measures": the new step is additive and advisory (always returns :ok), it does not wrap, reorder-around, or mask the exit code of either existing gate step, and neither existing step was weakened or removed. Not a gate-defeat.

No file outside handoffs/ was modified by this step. No source was edited -- this role gates, it does not fix.

issues.title: INV-1 Tenant data isolation -- APPLIES, PASS
issues.detail: APPLIES (not defaulted to NOT-APPLICABLE): S1 is done and S2 migrations exist per security-invariants.md's 2026-08-17 ISS-0026/GH#84 update, and lib/letflow/engine{,/transition,/reconstruction,/sub_process}.ex all reach tenant-scoped business tables. Verified per the invariant's own (a)/(b)/(c): (a) queries remain `:prefix`-scoped -- the diff adds NO query, and at every one of the sixteen sites the `prefix` parameter is passed through byte-identically (`_prefix`/`prefix` unchanged in all five reconstruction.ex apply_event/4 heads and in sub_process.ex:825's head); the schema-per-tenant mechanism of decision 0003 Dimension B is untouched. Confirmed empirically in the test log, where every engine query executes against a `tenant_<uuid>` schema prefix, never `public`. (b) NOT APPLICABLE within (a) -- the diff contains no migration and creates no table. (c) NOT APPLICABLE -- no `tenant_id` column is written or read by any changed line; no caller-supplied tenant attribution is introduced. Adding a struct pattern to a function head cannot widen a query's tenant scope. PASS.

issues.title: INV-2 Server-side field authorisation -- NOT-APPLICABLE
issues.detail: NOT-APPLICABLE. S4 has not started and the diff adds or changes no API response type, view module, Jason.Encoder derivation, or serialisation path. The only new output-producing code is lib/mix/tasks/letflow.check_toolchain.ex, which writes to a developer's stderr, not to a client response, and shapes no tenant-scoped entity.

issues.title: INV-3 Untrusted runtime sandboxing -- NOT-APPLICABLE
issues.detail: NOT-APPLICABLE. S5 (scripting/plugins) has not started, its build-vs-bind decision record does not exist, and the diff introduces no Lua, WASM, NIF, or Port surface and no tenant-authored script execution of any kind.

issues.title: INV-4 Secrets by reference only -- APPLIES, PASS
issues.detail: APPLIES via scope-test criterion (3), and assessed against the actual code of lib/mix/tasks/letflow.check_toolchain.ex rather than its stated intent, as the handoff required. WHAT IT READS: exactly one file, `Path.join(cwd, @pin_file)` where @pin_file is a compile-time module-attribute constant `.tool-versions` (:210), via `File.read/1` (:216). WHAT IT INTERPOLATES INTO OUTPUT: the running Elixir version (`System.version/0`, :194), the running OTP release (`:erlang.system_info(:otp_release)`, :195), the two parsed pin tokens, the resolved path, `inspect(reason)` on a File error, and -- the only echo of raw file bytes -- malformed lines re-printed by malformed_lines/1 (:365). All output goes to stderr via `IO.puts(:stderr, ...)` (:400). CAN THE LOOKUP BE REDIRECTED: no. `run/1` (:180) ignores its argument entirely (`_args`), so no CLI flag can retarget it; the filename is a constant, never derived from input; the only influence is the process cwd, which is the Mix project root and is already controlled by whoever invokes mix. SECRETS: confirmed by reading and by grep that the module contains no `System.get_env`, no `Application.get_env`, no config read, and no reference to any credential, token, password, or database URL -- it resolves no secret, so it cannot log, serialise, or leak one. The invariant's two heuristic greps were run over the changed and new files and returned no hits. PASS. One INFO-level observation, deliberately NOT raised as a finding: echoing malformed `.tool-versions` lines verbatim to a terminal would pass through ANSI escape sequences if that file were hostile -- but `.tool-versions` is a version-controlled repo file, and anyone able to write it can already execute arbitrary code through mix.exs, so this grants no capability an attacker would not already have. Not a defect.

issues.title: INV-5 Not-found/forbidden indistinguishability -- NOT-APPLICABLE
issues.detail: NOT-APPLICABLE. S4 has not started and the diff adds no lookup-by-ID endpoint and no externally observable response path. The Part C annotations are on private engine functions with no client-visible status code or body, so no cross-tenant probe signal can be introduced or altered by them.

issues.title: INV-6 New data-access paths prove their scoping -- APPLIES, PASS
issues.detail: APPLIES as the meta-invariant. The diff introduces no new data-access path (no new route, no new host function, no migration creating a business table), and this handoff is itself the artefact the invariant requires: a SECURITY-REVIEWER record with `status: PASS` that explicitly lists all of INV-1..INV-8 and states, for each, whether it applies and how it is satisfied. Satisfied not by 'it compiles and tests pass' but by the producer-trace closure recorded in result.summary for Part C and by the code reading recorded under INV-4. PASS.

issues.title: INV-7 No SQL string interpolation -- APPLIES, PASS
issues.detail: APPLIES (Ecto is in use and the changed engine modules issue queries). Ran the invariant's grep for `Repo.query` / `Ecto.Adapters.SQL` across every changed and new source file -- no hits. The diff adds no raw SQL, no string-built query, and no new query of any kind; the sixteen Part C changes are pattern annotations in function heads, `with` clauses and `case` clauses, and the new mix task performs no database access whatsoever. Existing queries in these modules remain `Ecto.Query` composition, parameterised by construction. PASS.

issues.title: INV-8 No unhandled crashes on realistic failure paths -- APPLIES, PASS
issues.detail: APPLIES, and is the invariant Part C bears on most directly, since the change ADDS pattern matches capable of raising where bare variables previously could not. Assessed rather than waved through. (1) Reachability: the full producer trace in result.summary closes for all four risk classes -- every value arriving at the sixteen sites is a struct literal built at a storage boundary (SnapshotWriter.deserialize_state/2), a seed constructor, or a value already struct-guarded upstream (Transition.transition/3 at transition.ex:175, engine.ex:1467). No realistic path, including the reconstruction-from-event-log and snapshot-deserialisation paths the handoff specifically named, delivers a non-struct. (2) Empirical: 372/372 engine tests and 1217/1230 full-suite assertions pass with zero MatchError, FunctionClauseError, or CaseClauseError, and the snapshot-seeded replay path is demonstrably exercised. (3) Isolation: per the invariant's own carve-out, engine execution is per-instance `:gen_statem` isolated via Letflow.ProcessInstance, so even an unreached raise here would crash one tenant's own instance under supervision rather than a shared process serving other tenants. (4) The new mix task is exemplary on this invariant: `File.cwd/0` and `File.read/1` rather than their bang forms, every File error branch handled explicitly (:198, :220, :228), and a `try/rescue/catch` wrapper at :181-187 that converts any unforeseen raise or throw into an advisory message -- `run/1` is @spec'd `:ok` and always returns it. PASS.

issues.title: Observation for REVIEWER (idiom gate), not a security finding
issues.detail: Part C's annotations are applied inconsistently between two adjacent functions: dispatch_parallel_gateway/4 (lib/letflow/engine/transition.ex:605) annotates both `%InstanceState{} = instance_state` and `%Token{} = token`, while the function it immediately delegates to, dispatch_parallel_split/4 (lib/letflow/engine/transition.ex:656), annotates only instance_state and leaves `token` bare. Behaviourally harmless -- neither can receive a non-struct -- and outside this gate's remit. Recorded here so REVIEWER can decide at the idiom gate whether the convention should be uniform; not filed as a separate issue, since it is a property of the change under review and not an independent defect.

result.next_action: Proceed to the next WF-03 step (REVIEWER idiom gate, then TEST-RUNNER at Step 4). No rework required from ELIXIR-DEV: no applicable invariant failed, and Part C's behaviour-preservation claim was independently verified by producer trace and by a full test run rather than accepted. ORCH should note that the 13 full-suite failures (3 in Mix.Tasks.Letflow.Check.TestTest, 10 in Letflow.IdentityMigrationTest) were observed but deliberately not attributed here -- that is TEST-RUNNER's Step 4 work; the only claim this gate makes about them is that none touches the four engine modules changed by Part C. ORCH also still owns updating handoffs/registry.json for this step.
